newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Eurostat clears some EMU investment treatment.
newsitem.headline: Eurostat clears some EMU investment treatment.

text.p: Eurostat cleared on Friday the statistical treatment of a number of investments made by companies in public infrastructure.
The decision referred to specific cases concerning Germany, Denmark, Sweden and Britain.

Eurostat said the amounts involved were already correctly accounted for in the notifications sent by European Union member states to the European Commission twice a year in the framework of the excessive deficit procedure.

At issue was whether an investment for public infrastructure carried out by a company at the request of a government should be recorded in the general government sector for purposes of qualifying for economic and monetary union (EMU).
Eurostat described two separate cases, including one in which the investment contributed to an increase in the government deficit and the other in which it had no effect.
"Eurostat confirms...the treatment described above, and recorded as such in the accounts of Germany, Denmark, Sweden and the United Kingdom," a statement said. --Brussels newsroom +32 2 287-6830
